```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
```

MoFIA fits moderated nonlinear factor analysis (MNLFA) models (Bauer & Hussong,
2009; Bauer, 2017): factor models in which item parameters (loadings,
thresholds or intercepts, residual variances) and factor parameters (means,
variances, correlations) depend on moderators such as age or gender. Moderators
can be continuous or categorical, and there can be any number of them, so
measurement invariance and differential item functioning (DIF) can be tested
without forming groups. Estimation is by marginal maximum likelihood.

## Data

The `parabelief` data contain 14 paranormal-belief items, rated from 1
(*definitely not*) to 5 (*definitely*), for 600 Dutch respondents, together
with standardized age and gender (Hoogeveen et al., 2024). Here we analyse the
six items on belief in *unearthly beings*. Their answers are strongly skewed,
so we treat them as ordinal.

```{r}
library(MoFIA)
data(parabelief)
ub <- c("SpiritsGhosts", "GnomesElves", "Aliens", "DevilPossession",
        "Sorcery", "HauntedPlaces")
sapply(parabelief[ub], function(x) round(prop.table(table(x)), 2))
```

## The model

For a person with moderator values `x` (a row vector, no intercept) and one
factor `η`:

```
factor:           η ~ N(x'γ, exp(x'δ))
ordinal item j:   P(y_j ≥ k) = F(x'β_j + λ_j(x) η − τ_jk)
continuous item:  y_j ~ N(ν0_j + x'β_j + λ_j(x) η, exp(ω0_j + x'ω_j))
loadings:         λ_j(x) = λ0_j + x'λ1_j
```

`F` is the logistic distribution function (`link = "probit"` in `mofia()`
gives the normal). Every parameter is linear in the moderators, variances on
the log scale. The baseline parameters (`τ`, `λ0`, `ν0`, `ω0`) describe a
person with all moderators at 0, whose factor has mean 0 and (by default)
variance 1. In
`parabelief`, Age is standardized and Male is 0 for women, so this baseline
person is a woman of average age. For a moderator such as age in years, 0 lies
outside the data; centre it or use `standardize = TRUE` so that the baseline
describes a typical person. A positive `β_j` makes higher categories
of item `j` more likely at the same factor value: all its thresholds shift down
by the same amount (uniform DIF).

## Specifying a model

`mofia_model()` sets up the model and `mofia()` fits it. Item-level moderation
accepts `TRUE` (all items, all moderators), `FALSE`/`NULL`, item names (these
items, all moderators), a named list such as `list(Aliens = "Male")`, or a
logical matrix; for factor-level moderation a character vector names
moderators (see `?mofia_model`).

| Argument | Parameters | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `loading_mod` | `lambda1[item,factor,mod]` | none | loadings depend on `x` |
| `threshold_mod` | `beta[item,mod]` | none | ordinal items: one shift of all thresholds per item and moderator; continuous items: the intercept |
| `resvar_mod` | `omega[item,mod]` | none | log residual variances; continuous items only |
| `mean_mod` | `gamma[factor,mod]` | all moderators | factor means |
| `var_mod` | `delta[factor,mod]` | all moderators | log factor variances |
| `cor_mod` | `zcor1[f1,f2,mod]` | none | factor correlations, on the Fisher-z scale |
| `cov_param` | `zcor0`/`zcor1` or `cov0`/`cov1` | `"fisherz"` | `"linear"`: moderate covariances instead |
| `continuous` | `nu0`, `omega0` instead of `tau` | none | items treated as normal |
| `identification` | `delta0` (marker only) | `"variance"` | baseline factor variance 1, or `"marker"`: one loading per factor (`markers`) fixed to 1 |
| `standardize` | | `FALSE` | z-scores for continuous moderators; effects per SD |

Thresholds are `tau[item,k]`, baseline loadings `lambda0[item,factor]`.
Category-specific threshold DIF is not part of the model, so tests of `beta` do
not test it.

## Anchors and three nested models

Fixing the baseline mean and variance is not enough. If the factor mean and the
thresholds of *all* items depend on Age, a higher factor mean for older people
cannot be told apart from all thresholds shifting together; likewise, a
moderated factor variance cannot be told apart from all loadings changing
together. Since `mean_mod` and `var_mod` include all moderators by default, at
least one item per factor and moderator must keep invariant parameters: an
anchor. `mofia_model()` refuses exactly unidentified patterns and warns about
weakly identified ones. Moderating the loadings too does not help: for a binary
moderator, their products with the mean moderation are again absorbed by the
thresholds.

Here we choose `SpiritsGhosts` as the anchor; the score tests below examine
that choice. The anchor defines the scale of all comparisons: `gamma` is the
factor-mean difference as measured by the anchor, and every `beta` is DIF
*relative to the anchor*. If the anchor itself has DIF, that DIF passes into
`gamma` and, scaled by the loadings, into all `beta`. Three nested models:

* **scalar**: no item parameter is moderated;
* **metric**: the thresholds of all items except the anchor are moderated;
* **configural**: in addition, the loadings of all items except the anchor are moderated.

```{r}
others <- setdiff(ub, "SpiritsGhosts")
m_scalar <- mofia_model(parabelief, items = ub, moderators = c("Age", "Male"))
m_metric <- mofia_model(parabelief, items = ub, moderators = c("Age", "Male"),
                        threshold_mod = others)
m_config <- mofia_model(parabelief, items = ub, moderators = c("Age", "Male"),
                        threshold_mod = others, loading_mod = others)
m_metric
```

## Fitting and checking the fit

```{r}
scalar <- mofia(m_scalar)
metric <- mofia(m_metric)
config <- mofia(m_config)
metric
```

The factor is integrated out by adaptive Gauss-Hermite quadrature (31 nodes
for one factor). The check in parentheses recomputes the log-likelihood with a
finer rule; if it changes by more than `accuracy` (0.005), `mofia()` refits with
the finer rule and warns if that does not settle it (then increase `nq`).
"Converged" means that the information matrix is positive definite (a maximum,
identified by these data) and that the Newton decrement, the log-likelihood
still to be gained by one more Newton step, is below `1e-6`. If not:

* `status` `"saddle"`: not a maximum; no standard errors or tests. Try random
  starts (`starts = 5`, with a seed).
* `status` `"singular"`: not identified by these data; check the anchors.
* positive definite but a large decrement: standard errors come with a warning,
  and Wald, likelihood-ratio and score tests are refused.
* an error "Estimation failed: ..." (class `"mofia_estimation_error"`): no
  regular maximum, typically because the model is not identified.

Details: `metric$status`, `$se_note`, `$quadrature`.

## Comparing models

```{r}
anova(scalar, metric, config)
```

Each row tests a model against the one above it. `Chisq` is the Satorra-Bentler
(2001) scaled difference statistic: the likelihood-ratio statistic divided by
`Scaling`, the scaling factor of the difference, computed from the models'
robust scaling factors (`metric$scaling`). These are close to 1 when the
distributional assumptions hold; when `Scaling` is above 1, the unscaled test
(`scaled = FALSE`) would be too liberal. In small samples it can be negative
(*p* = `NA`); `mofia_lrt(fit0, fit1, sb2010 = TRUE)` adds the always positive
Satorra-Bentler (2010) version.

Moderating the thresholds improves the fit clearly, so at least some items show
threshold DIF. Moderating the loadings does not improve it further, and AIC and
BIC also prefer the metric model: there is no evidence of loading DIF.

A Wald test needs only the larger model and tests any set of parameters, named
or matched by a regular expression: one item's DIF, and all Age DIF:

```{r}
mofia_wald(metric, "^beta\\[DevilPossession,", regex = TRUE)
mofia_wald(metric, "^beta\\[.*,Age\\]$", regex = TRUE)
```

## Score tests: screening all items at once

Like modification indices, `mofia_score_test()` tests, from one fit, every
moderation effect the model lacks. `statistic` is the robust score statistic
(Boos, 1992), `statistic_ML` the model-based one; `p_adj` is Holm-adjusted
across all rows. `by = "item"` pools each item's threshold or loading effects
over the moderators:

```{r}
screen <- mofia_score_test(scalar, by = "item")
screen[, c("test", "df", "statistic", "p", "p_adj")]
```

The screen flags threshold DIF for Aliens, DevilPossession and SpiritsGhosts
(adjusted *p* < .05) and no loading DIF, in line with the model comparisons.
The default `by = "parameter"` gives one test per effect with its expected
parameter change (`epc`), the approximate estimate if the effect were added:

```{r}
mi <- mofia_score_test(metric)
mi[grepl("Aliens|SpiritsGhosts", mi$test), c("test", "statistic", "p_adj", "epc")]
```

No loading effect survives the adjustment. The anchor's own threshold effects
are `NA`: adding them would remove the anchor, so they are not identified.

The scalar screen also flagged the anchor. Such tests are relative to the other
items, so this does not prove DIF, but it calls for a sensitivity analysis with
GnomesElves, the item with the weakest evidence, as anchor:

```{r}
metric_ge <- mofia(mofia_model(parabelief, items = ub, moderators = c("Age", "Male"),
                               threshold_mod = setdiff(ub, "GnomesElves")))
c(SpiritsGhosts = logLik(metric), GnomesElves = logLik(metric_ge))
rbind(SpiritsGhosts = coef(metric)[c("gamma[eta,Age]", "gamma[eta,Male]")],
      GnomesElves = coef(metric_ge)[c("gamma[eta,Age]", "gamma[eta,Male]")])
```

The fit is identical: with one anchor and invariant loadings, the anchor only
moves effects between `gamma` and the `beta`, and the data cannot tell which
anchor is right. The conclusions differ: measured by GnomesElves, the age
decline of the factor mean is about a third as large, and the rest counts as
item DIF. Choosing anchors from the same data and then testing on them is
post-selection inference (the Holm adjustment covers only the screen). Base
anchors on substantive arguments or independent data, and report how much the
results depend on them.

## Parameter estimates

`summary()` prints all estimates grouped by type; the table can be used
directly:

```{r}
est <- summary(metric)$coefficients
est[est$type %in% c("beta", "gamma", "delta"), c("estimate", "se", "z", "p")]
```

Names give the type and its indices, e.g. `beta[item,moderator]` (all types
under *Parameter names* in `?mofia_model`). With the logit link:

* `beta[Aliens,Male]` = 1.08: at the same factor value, men's odds of answering
  in a higher category on Aliens are exp(1.08) ≈ 2.9 times women's;
* `gamma[eta,Male]` = −0.65: men's factor mean is 0.65 baseline SDs lower;
* `delta[eta,Male]` = 0.42: men's factor SD is exp(0.42 / 2) ≈ 1.23 times
  women's.

Standard errors are robust (MLR) by default: a sandwich with the exact observed
information, which protects them against misspecified distributions (it does
not make a misspecified moderation effect the quantity of scientific interest).
`se = "ML"` (inverse information) and `se = "MLF"` (outer product of the scores)
assume a correct model. `information = "reduced"` drops the curvature of the
nonlinear transformations (log variances, Fisher z); it is consistent only
under correct specification and mainly useful to compare with software that
computes standard errors this way. `summary()`, `vcov()`, `confint()` and
`mofia_wald()` take both arguments; `anova()` and `mofia_lrt()` take
`information`.

## Plots, factor scores and predictions

`plot()` shows how the factor mean and SD change with a moderator, how
moderated loadings change, or item response functions at several moderator
values (DIF shows as curves that differ). Bands are pointwise; the factor bands
have zero width at the baseline, where mean and variance are fixed:

```{r, fig.width = 7, fig.height = 3.5}
plot(metric, "factors", moderator = "Age")
plot(metric, "items", moderator = "Male", items = c("DevilPossession", "Aliens"))
```

`mofia_scores()` gives EAP factor scores with posterior SDs, on the scale of
the model's factor (so they include the moderated means and variances) and
conditional on the estimates (the SDs omit estimation uncertainty); attribute
`"row_index"` matches them to the rows of the data. `predict()` gives expected
item scores (or, with `type = "prob"`, category probabilities) for new moderator
values on their original scale, averaged over the factor distribution at those
values:

```{r}
head(mofia_scores(metric), 3)
predict(metric, newdata = data.frame(Age = c(-1, 1), Male = c(0, 1)))
```

## Continuous items

Items can also be treated as normal (`continuous`). `threshold_mod` then
moderates their intercepts. Their residual variances are not moderated unless
`resvar_mod` says so; it takes the same forms as `threshold_mod`, acts on the
log residual variances (`omega`) and is refused for categorical items:

```{r}
m_cont <- mofia_model(parabelief, items = ub, moderators = c("Age", "Male"),
                      threshold_mod = others, continuous = ub)
m_cont_rv <- mofia_model(parabelief, items = ub, moderators = c("Age", "Male"),
                         threshold_mod = others, continuous = ub, resvar_mod = TRUE)
cont <- mofia(m_cont)
cont_rv <- mofia(m_cont_rv)
anova(cont, cont_rv)
c(continuous = cont$scaling[["exact"]], ordinal = metric$scaling[["exact"]])
```

Moderated residual variances improve the fit somewhat. The robust scaling
factor of the continuous model is well above 1, unlike the ordinal model's, a
sign that the normal model does not describe these skewed ratings well. Ordinal
and continuous items can also be mixed in one model.

## Formulas and model syntax

Moderators can also be given as a formula: factor variables are dummy-coded,
and interactions and transformations are allowed. `standardize = TRUE` turns
continuous moderators into z-scores (new data for `predict()` and plots stay on
the original scale). The loading pattern can be written in lavaan style:

```{r}
m_f <- mofia_model(parabelief, loadings = "UB =~ SpiritsGhosts + GnomesElves + Aliens +
                                           DevilPossession + Sorcery + HauntedPlaces",
                   moderators = ~ Age * Male, standardize = TRUE)
m_f$moderators
```

## More than one factor

For several factors, give the loading pattern as a named list or as model
syntax. With two factors, the factor correlation can be moderated as well
(`cor_mod`). Here all thresholds are moderated, so the factor means are not
(`mean_mod = FALSE`). Not run (it takes longer):

```{r, eval = FALSE}
eha <- c("HealingHands", "LifeCoursePossessions", "Graphology", "Dowsing",
         "MindReading", "Willpower", "SeeingFuture", "SeeingEvents")
m2 <- mofia_model(parabelief, loadings = list(EHA = eha, UB = ub),
                  moderators = c("Age", "Male"),
                  threshold_mod = TRUE, mean_mod = FALSE, cor_mod = TRUE)
fit2 <- mofia(m2, threads = 4)
```

Several threads need a build with OpenMP support (not the default Apple clang on
macOS); otherwise `mofia()` says so and computes serially. With three or more
factors, moderated correlations are refused unless `experimental_cor = TRUE`:
pairwise moderated correlations need not form a valid correlation matrix for
all moderator values, and this case is not yet methodologically established.

## Other helpers

* `mofia_collapse()` merges sparse categories (`mofia_model()` warns about
  categories with fewer than `sparse = 5` responses). This changes the
  measurement model, so report it.
* `mofia_drop()` removes named moderation effects, e.g. to build the restricted
  model for a likelihood-ratio test.
* `mofia_simulate()` draws data from a fitted or specified model, e.g. for power
  analyses or to check parameter recovery.
* `mofia_loglik()` evaluates the log-likelihood at given parameter values
  (e.g. estimates from other software) or with more quadrature nodes.
* `tidy()` and `glance()` return the estimates and a one-row model summary as
  data frames (with the generics or broom package loaded).

## Recommended workflow

1. Inspect category frequencies; collapse sparse categories if needed.
2. Give continuous moderators a meaningful zero (`standardize = TRUE`).
3. Choose anchors on substantive grounds, before looking at DIF tests.
4. Fit scalar, metric and, if needed, configural models; check convergence and
   the quadrature check.
5. Compare them with `anova()`; test sets of effects with `mofia_wald()`.
6. Screen with `mofia_score_test()`; treat flagged effects as hypotheses and
   check the sensitivity to the anchor.
7. Interpret `beta`, `gamma` and `delta` relative to the baseline person.
8. Report the anchors, collapsed categories, the link and the tests used.
